title: Renewal risk: metric matrix + KPI tracker (cheatsheet)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact working cheat-sheet used by CSMs and renewal engineers to: 1) standardize how we calculate QBR operational metrics tied to renewal risk, 2) provide simple numeric thresholds and suggested actions, and 3) act as an ingestable table for renewal tracker spreadsheets and customer decks.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally terse – operational teams want crisp, actionable signals, not long-winded definitions.

Metric definitions (canonical)
1) P95 request latency (ms)
   - Definition: 95th percentile end-to-end server-side generation latency for production text generation requests. Excludes cold-starts and non-user-initiated background jobs.
   - Measurement window: rolling 7d and 28d aggregates reported in QBR.
   - Calculation rules: compute per-route P95 from raw request latencies; if route-level sample < 100 requests/day, fallback to model-level P95.
   - Typical thresholds (renewal signaling):
       - Green: P95 <= 350ms
       - Yellow: 350ms < P95 <= 700ms (investigate batching/config, check region routing)
       - Red: P95 > 700ms (escalate to SRE & infra; possible dedicated capacity recommendation)

2) Uptime (availability) - customer-facing SLA footprint
   - Definition: percentage of successful requests over attempted requests for production tokens in the measurement window. Success = 200-series response with final model completion (no application-level error).
   - Window: monthly (30d) with QBR reporting on last 90d trend.
   - Calculation nuance: exclude planned maintenance windows (pre-agreed) and transient throttling responses counted as client-side rate limits.
   - Thresholds:
       - Green: >= 99.95%
       - Yellow: 99.50% <= uptime < 99.95%
       - Red: uptime < 99.50%
   - Action: any red -> require incident summary and remediation plan in the QBR appendix.

3) Cost per 1k tokens (USD)
   - Definition: total billed inference cost attributed to the customer divided by (tokens_generated + tokens_consumed) * 1000. Use invoice-level numbers where available; otherwise use telemetry cost-allocation model.
   - Window: monthly and trailing 90d average in QBR.
   - Calculation notes: include dedicated reservation amortization if customer uses Redwood Dedicated; exclude 3rd-party downstream charges. Include cache-savings as negative adjustments where applicable.
   - Threshold guidance (for renewal conversation):
       - Green: within +/-10% of expected benchmark for similar workload (see internal benchmark catalog id BENCH-LLM-001)
       - Yellow: 10–30% above benchmark (run cost optimization playbook)
       - Red: >30% above benchmark (consider quantization, caching, reroute to cheaper variant)

4) Prefix cache hit rate (% of tokens or requests)
   - Definition: percent of requests where the runtime served a cached KV/prefix chunk that avoided full model compute. Two calculation flavors: by request (request-level hit if any prefix cached) and by token (token-level saved tokens / total tokens).
   - Measurement: surface both request-hit% and token-saved% in the QBR.
   - Thresholds (workload dependent):
       - Green: request-hit >= 40% OR token-saved >= 30% (highly cacheable workloads)
       - Yellow: request-hit 15–40% OR token-saved 10–30%
       - Red: request-hit < 15% AND token-saved < 10% (low reuse: investigate prompt engineering or client-side prefixing)

Operational KPIs and how to present them in a QBR slide/table
- Use a single consolidated table per customer showing current window (30d), trailing 90d average, trend (▲/▼/–), and action column. Example table layout (plaintext; import-friendly):

Customer KPI snapshot (example rows)
| metric | 30d value | 90d avg | trend | status | recommended action |
| P95 latency (ms) | 480 | 420 | ▲ | yellow | increase burst capacity; check batching config |
| Uptime (%) | 99.87 | 99.92 | ▼ | yellow | run post-mortem for repeated 503s; add fallback route |
| Cost per 1k tokens (USD) | 3.42 | 2.95 | ▲ | red | run Optimize playbook: quantize, reduce max tokens |
| Cache request-hit (%) | 22 | 28 | ▼ | yellow | review prompt canonicalization; add client-side caching |

Customer renewal risk matrix (quick heuristic)
- Low risk: all green OR at most one yellow with strong product/usage signals.
- Medium risk: >=1 yellow and no reds, or >1 yellow.
- High risk: any red OR cost increases >30% with no remediation plan.

Suggested automations / queries to populate tracker (short)
- p95_latency_7d(route) -> aggregate, tag by model + region
- uptime_monthly(customer_id) -> exclude maintenance windows
- cost_allocated_monthly(customer_id) -> map billing -> tokens
- cache_hits_request_and_token(customer_id, 30d) -> separate columns for request_hit% and token_saved%

Playbook snippets (CS uses these in follow-ups)
- If P95 goes yellow: check recent model change PRs, inspect batching settings, validate region routing (fallthrough to cheaper model possible). Capture expected impact and next check-in date.
- If cost per 1k tokens spikes >10% month-over-month: run cost root-cause: model size change, prompt length, traffic shape. Propose quick wins: reduce max_tokens, lower temperature for sampling, enable prefix caching for repetitive prompts.
- If cache hit rate is low but usage patterns indicate repeatable prompts: create canonical prompt templates for clients or recommend client-side tokenization + prefixing.

QBR slide checklist (what to include)
- One-liner summary of risk (low/medium/high) + primary driver (latency/cost/uptime/cache).
- KPI table (30d, 90d avg, trend, status).
- Top 3 actions with owners and ETA.
- Supporting artifacts: incident links, Optimize playbook runbook, infra tickets.

Template tracker rows (CSV-friendly)
customer_id,customer_name,owner,p95_30d_ms,p95_90d_ms,uptime_30d,uptime_90d,cost_per_1k_30d,cost_per_1k_90d,cache_req_hit_30d,cache_token_saved_30d,status,risk_level,comments,action_owner,action_eta,linked_incident
12345,FinAI,Sam.Lee,480,420,99.87,99.92,3.42,2.95,22,12,yellow,medium,latency & cost skew,Miguel T,2026-03-07,INC-2026-004

Open questions / TODOs (notes for next iteration)
- Do we surface P99 for burst-sensitive customers? (probably add as optional column)
- Standardize tariff mapping for Dedicated amortized costs (accounting owns final calc).
- Add small visualization examples for the console (sparklines).

Appendix: common definitions (short)
- "tokens": sum of input tokens + output tokens counted via our tokenizer.
- "planned maintenance": windows agreed in contract and recorded in the customer calendar; needs ticket id.
- "expected benchmark": derived from model catalog + workload cluster (low-latency chat vs bulk generation).

End of cheat-sheet.

Revision log:
- 2025-11-10: initial working draft (Sam Lee)
- 2026-01-12: added cache token-level guidance (Asha)
- 2026-02-20: updated thresholds and added tracker CSV example (Miguel)
